text: Ninsun used the measuring rod to test the width and depth of the three lower marks. Their differences were slight but consistent, each cut narrowing as it descended, shaped by repeated blows from a small chisel held at an angle. Balag pointed out where the tool had slipped and been corrected. Ninsun found a section where the mason had deepened one side to compensate for a flaw in the stone. The marks had seemed crude when read as symbols. Examined as work, they became evidence of a careful hand.

text: Its width did not change. Its depth remained identical from the upper line to the open circle below, though there were no fractures along its edges and no roughness at the bottom.
